body:
After some confusion, I've gone through each case of these cases, both for "supports indexed properties" and "has indexed property setter" and tested against WPT and implementations, see below:


### [[Delete]]
https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-platform-object-delete

```js
localStorage.setItem("1", "someValue");
console.log(localStorage["1"])
console.log(delete localStorage[1])
console.log(localStorage.getItem("1"));
```

Gives:

| Test                | Result             |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Safari             | "someValue", true, null  |
| Chrome         | "someValue", true, null  |
| Firefox           | "someValue", true, null  |
| Spec without indexed storage | "someValue", true, null  |
| Spec with indexed storage | "someValue", false, "someValue"  |


### [[DefineOwnProperty]]

https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-platform-object-defineownproperty

```js
let desc = {
    value: "value",
};
Object.defineProperty(localStorage, 1, desc)
console.log(localStorage.getItem("1"));
```

| Test                | Result             |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Safari             | "value"  |
| Chrome         | "value"  |
| Firefox           | "value"  |
| Spec with indexed storage | "value"  |
| Spec without indexed storage | null  |

### [[GetOwnProperty]]

https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#PlatformObjectGetOwnProperty

```js
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(localStorage, 1));
localStorage.setItem("1", "value");
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(localStorage, 1));
```

| Test                | Result             |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Safari             | undefined, Object{ "value": "value", "writable": true, "enumerable": true, "configurable": true }  |
| Chrome         | undefined, Object{ "value": "value", "writable": true, "enumerable": true, "configurable": true }  |
| Firefox           | undefined, Object{ "value": "value", "writable": true, "enumerable": true, "configurable": true } |
| Spec with indexed storage | undefined, Object{ "value": "value", "writable": true, "enumerable": true, "configurable": true }  |
| Spec without indexed storage | undefined, Object{ "value": "value", "writable": true, "enumerable": true, "configurable": true } |


Second test, taken from [WPT](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/fc82c86dbd0daa98f645c3a309baac3665ecc706/webstorage/set.window.js#L33):

```js
var proto = "proto for sessionStorage";
Storage.prototype[9] = proto;

var value = "value for sesionStorage";

var storage = sessionStorage;
storage.clear();

console.log(storage[9]);

storage[9] = value;

console.log(storage[9]);
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(storage, 9));
```

| Test                | Result             |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Safari             | proto, proto, undefined  |
| Chrome         | proto, backing, undefined   |
| Firefox           | proto, proto, undefined   |
| Spec with indexed storage | proto, backing, Object{ "value": "backing", "writable": true, "enumerable": true, "configurable": true } |
| Spec without indexed storage | proto, proto, undefined   |


### [[OwnPropertyKeys]]

https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-platform-object-ownpropertykeys

```js
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(localStorage));
localStorage.setItem("0", "value");
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(localStorage));
```

| Test                | Result             |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Safari             | [], [ "0" ]  |
| Chrome         | [], [ "0" ]   |
| Firefox           | [], [ "0" ]   |
| Spec with indexed storage | [], [ "0", "0" ] |
| Spec without indexed storage | [], [ "0" ]   |

### Summary

So I suspect should be changed is something along the lines of:
- Storage object in HTML spec have indexed/named/etc property getters defined
- Storage object (somehow) defined to "supports indexed properties" codepath for [[DefineOwnProperty]]
- Storage object (somehow) defined so that "supports indexed properties" codepath is not taken in [[GetOwnProperty]], [[Delete]] and [[OwnPropertyKeys]]

I believe the above should align the spec with WPT, but there would still be 4 tests in https://wpt.fyi/results/webstorage/set.window.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned which all implementations do not agree with that I don't quite understand. Maybe that is still fine though?

`localStorage[9] = "some value"` calls [PutValue](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-putvalue) with V being a reference record representing `localStorage[9]` and W being `"some value"`. Step 3.c of that algorithm converts `9` to the string `"9"`. Then in [[Set]], because P is a string, it invokes the named property setter.

Oh jeez, I see where I went wrong.. Yep, PropertyKey can only be a String or a Symbol, and my mental model had it so that [is an array index](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#is-an-array-index) was independent of the string check in [[Set]]... That explains it.

I'll leave this open as I think I'll raise a MR to define the named property getters etc for Storage, but I think I've got it now
